speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you've had any recent head injuries, neck pain, or a stiff neck along with your fever and altered mentation?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall if you've taken more than the prescribed dose of haloperidol recently, or have you experienced any muscle stiffness or a high fever that feels uncontrollable? I also need to ask if you've had any recent exposure to insects or travel to areas with high mosquito activity.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of haloperidol use and symptoms like rigidity, profuse sweating, and altered mentation, I suspect Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Creatine Kinase, and Electrolytes.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: White Blood Cell Count 14,700/mm3 (elevated); Creatine Kinase: 5600 U/L (elevated); Electrolytes: Data not provided (Note: Serum Glucose 96 mg/dL and CSF Glucose 64 mg/dL available from Lumbar Puncture). Additional findings include Vital Signs: Temperature 39.6°C (103.2°F), Heart Rate 116/min; Lumbar Puncture: CSF Opening Pressure 22 cm H2O, WBC 4 cells/mm3, RBC 0 cells/mm3, Protein 48 mg/dL; Brain MRI: Unremarkable; Urine Toxicology: Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: The markedly elevated creatine kinase, high fever, and rigidity in the context of haloperidol use strongly confirm my suspicion. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
